body:
## Goal
Expose a small, dependency-free JSON REST API that lets each user sign up, sign in, view their identity, and create/list their own notes, with every account and note durably persisted to an on-disk store so all data survives a server restart.

## Spec
**Runtime & shape.** Node.js ESM (`"type": "module"`), server on the built-in `node:http` — **no external web framework** (Express/Fastify/etc. forbidden). Listens on `process.env.PORT`, default `3000`. All bodies are JSON; responses set `Content-Type: application/json`.

**Persistence (load-bearing: must survive restart).** State lives in an embedded on-disk store, not in memory — deliverer's choice of `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`, run under `--experimental-sqlite`) or an equivalent on-disk store (e.g. an fs-backed JSON file). The store file path derives from an env var with a repo-relative default and is gitignored. The store/schema is created on first run if absent (idempotent). All SQL (if used) MUST be parameterized — never concatenate user input.

**Endpoints.** `POST /signup` {username,password} → 201 {id,username}; duplicate username → 409. `POST /login` {username,password} → 200 {session} (opaque bearer credential); bad credentials → 401. `GET /me` (Bearer auth) → 200 {id,username}. `POST /notes` (authed) {title,body} → 201 with the created note owned by the caller. `GET /notes` (authed) → 200 JSON array of only the caller's notes.

**Auth & ownership (inviolable security invariants).** Passwords MUST be hashed (scrypt/bcrypt/argon2; `node:crypto` scrypt suffices) with a per-user salt — plaintext storage forbidden. Sessions are opaque high-entropy tokens (`crypto.randomBytes`) persisted and mapped to a user, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Protected endpoints reject missing/invalid tokens with 401. A user sees/mutates only their own notes (server-side scoping). Responses MUST exclude password hashes, salts, and raw session material beyond the `{session}` login returns. Never log passwords or session tokens. Auth endpoints carry a basic in-process rate limit.

**Bad-request handling.** Malformed JSON, missing/blank required fields, or wrong shape → 400 with a JSON error body. Unknown route → 404; unsupported method on a known path → 405. The server never crashes on bad input.

**Packaging.** Add an npm `start` script that launches the server (including any runtime flag the store needs). Ceilings: no explicit session expiry, no note update/delete, no HTTPS/CORS (see non-goals). The Authorization-header contract governs over the security baseline's cookie-storage default here.

## Changes
- `server.js` — creates
- `src/store.js` — creates
- `src/auth.js` — creates
- `package.json` — refactors-existing
- `.gitignore` — refactors-existing
- `test/api.test.js` — creates

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: `npm start` (PORT unset) launches an HTTP server listening on port 3000; setting PORT overrides it — and package.json declares no external web-framework dependency.
- [ ] AC-2: POST /signup with JSON {username,password} returns 201 and a JSON body containing the new user's id and username and no password hash/salt field; a second signup with the same username returns 409.
- [ ] AC-3: POST /login with correct {username,password} returns 200 and {session} (a non-empty opaque string); wrong password or unknown user returns 401.
- [ ] AC-4: GET /me with a valid Authorization: Bearer <session> returns 200 {id,username}; missing or invalid token returns 401.
- [ ] AC-5: POST /notes (authed) with {title,body} returns 201 with the created note; GET /notes (authed) returns a JSON array containing only the caller's notes and excluding notes created by a different user.
- [ ] AC-6: Malformed JSON or missing required fields return 400 with a JSON error body without crashing the server; an unknown route returns 404.
- [ ] AC-7: After stopping and restarting the server against the same store file, a previously signed-up user can still log in and a previously created note is still listed by GET /notes.
- [ ] AC-8: Passwords are never stored in plaintext — the on-disk store holds only a hash+salt, never the raw password.

## Verify
- npm start & then run an end-to-end curl/fetch script that signs up, logs in, calls /me, creates and lists notes, and asserts a second user's note is not visible to the first (e2e)
- node --test suite exercising signup→login→bearer→notes, ownership isolation, and the 400/401/404/409 error paths against a temp store file (contract)
- node --test unit tests for the password hash/verify helper and the JSON body parser/validator (unit)
- restart test: create data, terminate the process, relaunch against the same store file, assert prior user login and prior note both persist (contract)
- npm run lint (validate)

## Non-Goals
- No web UI, HTML rendering, or static asset serving.
- No note update/delete, sharing, pagination, or search.
- No password reset, email verification, refresh tokens, or session expiry beyond opaque-token validity.
- No HTTPS/TLS termination, CORS, or reverse-proxy configuration.
